content.text: As pointed out by Danny in the CLAW issue linked there, we
expect to see this attached to the /fcr:metadata, but as a <link rel="type"/> in its HTTP headers and not in the content (since the content is about the binary proper).
Currently a binary returns these <link rel="type"/>s in its headers
A binary description returns these <link rel="type"/>s in its headers.
So in the headers you have a correct separation of RDFSource and NonRDFSource. So I will just look at the RDF properties.

Is it easy to put it into the appropriate http headers? (I don't understand Fedora's architecture or where these different triples come from, but it seems like it should go in the headers of the binary description.
it is relatively easy to add it to the headers, but it is an internal "type" and so does not really mean anything outside of Fedora.
I would suggest that as the actual binary has a rel="describedby" header which points to the description, you are better to use that and treat the description like any other ldp:RDFSource object.
But maybe you have a use case for this fedora:* type?
It seems that the fedora:NonRdfSourceDescription triple is returned but the RDF is about the binary and so this seems incorrect.

comments.body: As pointed out by Danny in the CLAW issue linked there, we do expect to see this attached to the /fcr:metadata, but as a <link rel="type"/> in its HTTP headers and not in the content (since the content is about the binary proper).

Currently a binary returns these <link rel="type"/>s in its headers

Link: <http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#Resource>;rel="type"
Link: <http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#NonRDFSource>;rel="type"
Link: <http://mementoweb.org/ns#OriginalResource>; rel="type"
Link: <http://mementoweb.org/ns#TimeGate>; rel="type"

A binary description returns these <link rel="type"/>s in its headers.

Link: <http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#Resource>;rel="type"
Link: <http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#RDFSource>; rel="type"
Link: <http://mementoweb.org/ns#OriginalResource>; rel="type"
Link: <http://mementoweb.org/ns#TimeGate>; rel="type"

So in the headers you have a correct separation of RDFSource and NonRDFSource. So I will just look at the RDF properties.

Is it easy to put it into the appropriate http headers? (I don't understand Fedora's architecture or where these different triples come from, but it seems like it should go in the headers of the binary description.

Rosie Le Faive it is relatively easy to add it to the headers, but it is an internal "type" and so does not really mean anything outside of Fedora.

I would suggest that as the actual binary has a rel="describedby" header which points to the description, you are better to use that and treat the description like any other ldp:RDFSource object.

But maybe you have a use case for this fedora:* type?
